absent: Zone span test, early-initialized test, pageblock alignment and migration-type encoding beyond names used.
Allocator free path, buddy or slab behavior, reclaim scanning, and total RAM accounting beyond the call shown.
Memblock storage growth, node derivation, and flag semantics beyond the uses shown.
Handover transport, device-tree helpers, and address translation internals.
Control-group hierarchy, statistic layout, threshold registration, and swap accounting beyond the fragments.
Debug filesystem and sequence output helper behavior and operation tables.

findings.text: Public deferred page initializer accepts a frame number plus node id and forwards to an internal helper, allowing early boot code to complete descriptor setup lazily.
Deferred initialization is skipped when the frame was already set up early; otherwise the owning zone is located by scanning zones in order for span containment before single-page setup runs.
When the frame starts a pageblock, its migration grouping is initialized with a scratch-aware default for movable pages in non-overwrite mode.

Single-page setup establishes a clean descriptor: storage cleared, zone node and frame linkage recorded, reference count initialized, unmapped indicator set, tracking tags reset, idle list prepared, and direct-map address assigned for low zones where virtual addresses are kept.
One build variant of the deferred helper does nothing, so callers remain valid when deferred initialization is compiled out.

Reserved descriptor preparation first labels all regions with node ownership and marks no-map ranges reserved, restarting if the reserved array grew, then initializes only reserved ranges lacking the no-init marker, deriving missing node ids from early mapping.
Early low-memory release clears hotplug marks, prepares reserved descriptors, then walks free ranges outside any fixed node and accumulates the freed page count.
Managed page counters for every zone on every online node are zeroed exactly once per boot, guarded by a one-time flag that makes later calls return immediately.
Top-level early free routine discards unused descriptor storage, resets managed counters, disables scratch-only mode, frees low memory and adds the result to total RAM accounting.
A global scratch-only indicator is enabled and disabled by dedicated early helpers bracketing the handover window.
Named reservation table entry holds a short name plus physical start and length; the table is a fixed array with a live count protected by a mutex.
Named reservation table holds at most eight entries.
Reservation names are limited to sixteen bytes including termination.
Appending a reservation writes the next slot and bumps the count without internal bounds enforcement; lookup scans live entries, ignores zero-length slots, and matches by name equality.
Append relies on callers to check capacity first, so direct use without a room test would overflow the fixed table.
Name-based query returns start and length under mutex protection, reporting found versus missing with a boolean-style status.
Name-based release looks up under mutex, translates the range to virtual addresses, returns those pages to the allocator with a formatted tag, then clears the length to mark the slot free.
All name-table search, release and debug display paths hold the reservation mutex for the whole lookup and mutation sequence.
Preservation walks the reservation table preserving each range and on failure unpreserves the prefix already preserved before reporting the error.

Handover description build allocates one page, preserves it, emits a container with per-reservation children carrying start and length, registers the subtree, then preserves payloads, unwinding subtree, preservation and allocation on any failure stage.
Handover retrieval caches the description pointer, treats absence as non-fatal, warns on transport or compatibility failures, and discards incompatible descriptions.

Revival validates child presence, compatibility label, property lengths, requested alignment and exact size match before re-adding the prior reservation and logging success; any mismatch warns or fails silently and returns not-revived.
One build variant of revival always reports not-revived, forcing fresh allocation when handover lookup is unavailable.

Boot parameter handling parses length, alignment and name, enforces room, non-empty bounded name with visible text, uniqueness and minimum alignment, attempts handover revival first, otherwise allocates and records the reservation, with distinct errors for malformed input, exhaustion and allocation failure.

Memory-type flag labels cover hotplug, mirror, no-map, driver-managed, no-init reserved, kernel reserved, scratch and hugetlb reserved, with unknown bits shown as unknown and empty sets shown as none.
Debug listing prints per-region index, address interval, node id or placeholder, and bar-separated flag labels.
Debug filesystem exposure of memory arrays is present in one build variant and entirely absent in the other.
Reservation debug output lists only non-empty entries with human-scaled sizes under mutex; directory creation is skipped unless archival retention is enabled or reservations exist.
Per-node excess tree node keeps a red-black root, a cached rightmost pointer for extremum access, and a spinlock guarding updates.
Global soft-limit forest holds one per-node excess tree pointer per possible node, stored in mostly-read shared state.
Reclaim loop bound is one hundred iterations.
Soft-limit reclaim loop bound is two iterations.
Event file list element links notifications and holds the associated event file context.

Control-group event object binds an owning group, a signaling channel, list linkage, register and unregister callbacks, plus poll state, wait-queue linkage and deferred removal work for teardown on channel close.
File identifier packs a sixteen-bit type in the high half and a sixteen-bit attribute in the low half, with helpers to build and split the fields.
Resource counter kinds are ordered usage, limit, peak usage, then failure count.
Global out-of-memory serialization uses a dedicated spinlock described by its own lock dependency marker.
Removal from the excess tree is serialized by the per-node tree spinlock with interrupt state saved and restored across the update.
Group teardown walks every node and detaches that node accounting object from its excess tree when that tree exists.
Charge-migration control always reads zero; one build warns about deprecation and accepts only zero while rejecting other values, and the other build always reports not implemented.
Per-CPU event accounting keeps a page-event total plus one counter per notification target covering threshold and soft-limit kinds terminated by a count sentinel.
Threshold notification batch target is one hundred twenty eight and soft-limit batch target is one thousand twenty four.
Charge commit and batched uncharge update statistics and evaluate event thresholds with interrupts masked to keep per-CPU accounting consistent.
Swap-in path expects cache membership and locked state, and when combined memory-plus-swap accounting is active it must drop the duplicate swap charge promptly to avoid long-lived double counting.
Threshold ordering compares numeric limits with negative, zero and positive results for less, equal and greater.
Early boot interfaces for deferred page setup, single-page setup, full early release and managed-counter reset are visible outside their translation units.
Version-one control-group helpers for tree removal, charge commit, swap-in handling and batched uncharge are visible outside their translation unit.
